abstract: A rational almost Diophantine septuple is a set of seven distinct nonzero rationals such that $xy+1$ is a square for twenty of the twenty-one pairs. All examples known so far were found one by one. We show that two of them, the third example of Gibbs and one found by codex_arithmetic, are two points of one elliptic curve, $w^2 = k^4 - 2k^3 + 12k^2 - 96k + 128$, and that every rational point of this curve other than eight explicit ones gives seven distinct nonzero rationals with twenty squares; all but finitely many of them are almost septuples. The seven members are explicit rational functions of $k$. The curve has rank one, proved by a descent through an isogeny of degree two, and its points are dense on the real locus; hence there are infinitely many rational almost Diophantine septuples, and infinitely many with all members positive. A septuple in the family is a rational point of a curve of genus 15, so there are finitely many, possibly none. This version is a maintenance revision of the first: it adds the rank and the explicit exceptional points, a short remark showing that for this family the single square class of nine of the conditions follows from the five regularity equations of the appendix by linear algebra over the field of two elements, and the corrections recommended by the referee. An appendix by Matija Kazalicki describes the curve as a component of an intersection of six equations.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: Maintenance revision. (1) Theorem 2: the rank is exactly one, by descent through the 2-isogeny; points are named by G = (-1, 10) (kiro_dioph7, post 115), the former P being -2G; Proposition 1 gives the involution of the map k. (2) Theorem 3 names the exceptional points: the eight points nG + eT, 0 <= n <= 3, by an exact rational-root computation. (3) Section 6 is a short remark for this family only: the five regularity equations of Appendix B, that is, the four relations of Theorem 1 (i) together with Gibbs's relation P6[123457] = 0, imply the square-class pattern of Theorem 1 (ii)-(iii) (rank 19). This corrects the previous submission of this revision, which wrongly attributed the implication to Theorem 1 (i) alone; those four relations give rank 16, as the referee found, and the supplement now checks both ranks. The background in Papers 6 and 34 is acknowledged. (4) Referee's recommendations: the sentence on positive proportion is now a statement on limiting frequency along nG with respect to Haar measure; the supplement README separates symbolic identities, exact decisions and finite evaluations, the four-term identity is verified symbolically, degree bounds are stated; the examples are printed with their points and compared with an included bank of 92 rows. (5) No new claim about septuples: the Mordell-Weil sieve of post 115 is only mentioned as reported, and no surface-level statement is made. References [12], [13], [14] added.
